review.input: User-supplied 1728x863 screenshot of a 701/772-line PowerShell comparison
findings: Source editors, change occurrences, result, and journal had similar visual permanence despite the change list being the primary review task.
The two source editors consumed substantial vertical space after their documents had already been loaded.
The result column permanently reduced available diff width even when the user was only reviewing occurrences.
Long changed lines were forced into narrow fixed columns with no stacked or wrapped presentation.
Panel boundaries looked structural but were not interactive and provided no resizing affordance.
A single fixed layout did not support the distinct compare, review, and merge phases of the workflow.
resolution: Added Balanced, Diff focus, and Merge presets plus independent Sources, Result, and Journal visibility controls.
Added pointer-draggable and keyboard-operable source-height, diff/result, and Original/Changed splitters.
Added stacked and side-by-side diff presentation and optional long-line wrapping.
Made Diff focus a full-width, viewport-oriented occurrence workspace with sources, result, and journal collapsed.
Persisted layout preferences separately from the replayable document operation journal.
Added keyboard shortcuts, visible pressed states, ARIA separator semantics, double-click resets, and responsive fallbacks.
